for_the_reviewer:
"ONE THING TO CHALLENGE FIRST: your forced fix said 'one of the two moves, and one file changes', and four files of mine changed. The move is in one file - instrument/affordance.json - and agreement.py is untouched. The other three are the round's own rules, not extra fixing: criteria.json and marking-plan.md because a change to this instrument is recorded as an addendum with the date and the fault number and never silently, and four lines of code/marks.py because your fix also says 'Say in the counts file which of the two was done' and the counts file is not the instrument's to write. Those four lines carry no decision: they append affordance.json's own one-sentence `note_to_the_counts_file` to the `corpus_affordance_from` string agreement.py already prints. Delete the note from the table and the reading does not move (falsifier F-D); that is the test of the claim that they decide nothing.

WHY THE TABLE AND NOT agreement.py. Your fault says one shape carried two meanings. A rule in the reader that parses the row's `status` or `basis` leaves that shape standing and holds the fix by a form of words: F-D reworded every prose line of the retired row to near neighbours ('the corpus is silent about this one'), and under my move nothing changed, where under the status-reading move the exclusion would have come back - your fault again, wearing different words. F-E is the other half: put `affords: []` back on the row and keep every word of its prose, and the field is excluded again. So the shape, and only the shape, is what the harness reads, which is what I wanted holding the fix.

WHERE TO POINT YOUR OWN RUN. agreement.run_agreement with the real criteria.json over any marks set: fields.turned_own_test should read afforded=None, in_the_affordance_table=False; P4.2 and P4.3 should read over twelve certified cross-step fields including turned_own_test, and leave out test_patches alone, with corpus_affordance_from carrying the table's note. Two numbers to correct as you go: yours (and A4's round-2 note) say twelve read where thirteen should be; running it gives eleven and twelve, because same_explanation_quote is `text` and is never compared.

THE CHECK THAT REPLACES YOURS. 'Fourteen cross-step fields, fourteen rows, none missing' is the check that let this fault through - a row count cannot tell an exclusion from a gap. The check now is F-F, written into marking-plan 15.3: every cross-step field of criteria.json stands in exactly one of affordance.json's two lists, none in both, none in neither, and no row outside `fields` carries an `affords` key. It is also the gauge against what this move gives up: a row deleted by accident now makes a field read rather than making the harness complain.

WHAT DID NOT MOVE. criteria.json's `fields` array is byte-identical to W10-A4-3's, object for object: no criterion, value, quote, kind, sort or certified_candidate changed, so no quote sweep can have moved and W3 P3.4's rewording count does not move - section 14.4's count and its strict rule stand exactly as round 2 wrote them. On runs_sonnet5/F4-m2-r3.json, turned_own_test is N before and after, by clause (ii); what changed there is that the field is read at all.

ONE THING I COULD NOT SETTLE AND DID NOT PATCH. Whether turned_own_test has any purchase in the eight arms documents is still unknown: nobody on this round has read them and no text of them is in the repository. Reading the field is not a claim that it will vary - the 'never varies' flag is the gauge, and if it carries nothing the runs will show it. That is the difference between a gap and an exclusion, which is the whole of fault 28."
